name: Satyendra Nath Bose
role: Indian physicist, science educator and nominated Rajya Sabha member (1952–1958)
summary: Bose promoted accessible science education in Indian languages. His public addresses joined planned development and cultural pluralism with opposition to preventive detention.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: His writing hopes science will bring prosperity and end superstition but in 1969 says the moon voyage gave no clue to ending race, religion and colour discrimination and doubts that day will come.

revolution-justified.rationale: He honoured young revolutionaries who staked everything to free the country and himself helped the underground as a young man, but in 1971 told graduates that glorifying revolution is not enough and that hatred and violence cannot be its last word.

war-builds-character.rationale: He described the two world wars as savage destruction in which the lessons of science were used to exterminate mankind.

separate-church-state.rationale: In 1973 he called the news that Bangladesh would have a secular administration hopeful and described the Khilafat dream of a religious state as a divisive instrument; this is a short remark, not a developed argument.

ethnic-nation.rationale: He describes India as a single nation fused from many races and faiths, and wanted Hindus, Muslims and others to stand together irrespective of race or religion.

limit-population.rationale: In 1969 he said the alarming growth of population requires self-control and belief in family planning alongside raising harvests.

restore-past-order.rationale: Rejects old thinking for modern problems.

means-match-ends.rationale: In 1971 he asked whether killing those one cannot love is the new order, warning that such liquidation fills minds with hatred, though his youth record on violence is mixed.

return-to-foraging.rationale: In 1936 he said the remedy for failure is not a return to wilderness and ascetic, primitive pastoral life, and in 1962 that reverting to the past is no road to success.

hereditarian-race.rationale: In 1936 he called talk of race and congenital inferiority inane when blaming Indian youth, and in 1964 he described Nazi racism as monstrous.

national-self-determination.rationale: His convocation addresses celebrate breaking the shackles of foreign rule and sitting among free nations; this is stated for India and not argued as a general right.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: In the 1950s he wanted a university to preach the unity of men irrespective of caste, creed, religion, status or wealth, calling man the truth above everything.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: In 1962 he said cooperation instead of enmity and conflict is the directive of evolution's history, while noting wartime rivalry sped some science.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: In 1962 he argued English-educated leaders drifted from the people and kept most of them in ignorance, and called for the fruits of freedom to reach more than the educated few; this is about English-educated elites.

notes:
Nonviolence concerned domestic politics; later defense support is recorded. Collective ownership remains unspecified.

claude-sonnet-5-5 notes: Independent second pass (claude-sonnet-5-5) over his own collected addresses (1936-1973), Rajya Sabha speeches (1955-57) and a biography. He spoke little on economics, elections, courts or foreign policy, so those themes are null. Dropped from the earlier pass because no stated position settles them: central planning, state direction of investment, democracy, collective ownership, space expansion, fossil fuels, tariffs, minority languages and personal self-defence. Politics here was incidental to his science and language advocacy.
